_schema: THE TOWN'S PEOPLE. One record per person; npc.js reads it and owns no coordinate, name or behaviour of its own. FIELDS — id: unique key. name: the E-prompt name (the dialogue window's nameplate comes from dialogue.json's speaker table, not from here). scene: a scene key or a LIST of them; a town villager lives in both the real-time explore bundle (townwalk) and the cinematic one (del-cine), which share the same world coordinates because del-cine ships the whole town's collision. position: RUNTIME [x, height, -y] — the town map authors [x, across-gorge, height], so a map pos [80.73, 16, 14] is [80.73, 14, -16] here. Every position below is a vertex of the town's own derived walk network (townmap/dellhollow.routes.json), so nobody stands off the path. facing: THE POST YAW, in degrees about +Y — 0 looks down runtime +Z (which is map -Y: the near side of the gorge, the side the fixed cameras and the shop doors are on), 90 looks down +X. Same convention play3d turns the player with. Honoured by body.type 'model' AS A POST: a wander errand turns the body with its travel and the yaw eases back here when the errand ends. IGNORED by a billboard, which always turns to the camera. height: multiple of the engine's charH (MODEL_H, the [ / ] dial), so re-tuning the player re-tunes the town; a model with no height of its own takes defaults.adultHeight, so the grown-ups are not all exactly as tall as a nineteen-year-old. body.type: 'billboard' (a chroma-keyed pose plate, today) or 'model' (a GLB, the day one exists — npc.js already loads it). body.src: the plate, page-relative. body.tint: multiplies the plate, which is how the chapter-2 expansion script dresses a REUSED villager sheet as somebody else ('reuse the poppy sheet, tint #d9b08a'); see bodyNote for who is wearing whose coat. body.plate: the chroma-key plate a person wore BEFORE they were given a body — kept, unread by npc.js, so handing a body back is an edit to body.type and body.src alone. body.h: a MODEL's height multiple where it differs from the plate's (npc.js prefers it over the record's height). idleBehavior: 'stand' | 'lean' (a few degrees into whatever they lean on) | 'wander' (a small errand on the walk network, WALKLOCK semantics: a step that leaves the network or hits a wall ends the errand). radius: talk reach in metres. dialogue: a node id in game/dialogue.json. shop: a shops.json id — marks a keeper, whose greeting node opens the counter via its own effect, so the player is greeted and THEN traded with.
_canon: Cast, placement and voice are from docs/chapter2-dellhollow-script.md, docs/chapter2-expansion-script.md and docs/VOICES.md. Odessa's post is the lockhead ('the senior lockkeeper's working post' — the town map says so); she and Maren live at the Keepers' Cottage. Hobb is nineteen days into the stopped queue; Pell keeps the wicks; Sorrel prices everything; Creel splices what the town hangs from; Nib administers the gulls. The eel-wife and the boatwright are canon ROLES the scripts name without naming (a woman selling eels, the boatwright's shed) and carry title nameplates rather than invented names. Nobody here carries a plot fact and nobody says the word 'afraid'.
_artNote: Only ten characters in public/assets/char-manifest.json ship a keyed pose plate, and five of these villagers (Hobb, Pell, Sorrel, Creel, Nib) are specified in the scripts as sprite-first, nameplate-only extras on REUSED, TINTED villager sheets. bodyNote records the loan for the art pipeline: replace src (and drop tint) the day the character is drawn, and nothing else changes. 2026-07-31: seven of them wore a rigged GLB (body.type 'model'), retargeted from the four Tripo deliveries finn/mara/maren/pip by tools/vesper_retarget.py's NPC recipe (Walk_Loop, not the player's jog); body.plate keeps the plate each of them wore, so the loan is still recorded and still reversible.
_bodies: EVERY PERSON IS A BODY (user ruling, 2026-08-01, after playing: 'swap those all out for the existing 3D models, even if we have to reuse them a bunch of times'). There is no human billboard left in either town. Four rigged GLBs carry all of them — finn (adult man), mara (adult woman), maren (young woman), pip (child) — and the variation is body.tint and body.h, which is the SAME device the expansion script already licensed for the plates ('reuse the poppy sheet, tint it'), now worn by a mesh instead of a texture. TWO BILLBOARDS SURVIVE AND BOTH ARE THE CAT: there is no quadruped model, and a human GLB squashed to 0.30 charH is a worse defect than the plate it replaced (a tiny person, not a cat). Mochi keeps his plate in both towns until a cat is delivered; that exception was ratified by the coordinator in the same pass. HEIGHT IS THE OTHER HALF OF THE VARIATION: defaults.adultHeight 1.10 is the standard grown-up, and a record states its own body.h only when the person is not one — 1.13 for a tall senior, 1.05 for a stooped old man, 0.70-0.76 for the children. A street where everyone is exactly 1.10 reads as one model pasted eleven times, which is the thing this ruling was issued against.
_posts: NOBODY STANDS WHERE THE PLAYER MATERIALISES (rule earned 2026-08-01, by measurement, from a transition_test failure that turned out not to be about people at all). Every arrival in public/world/scenegraph.json carries a `spawn`, and a door, a seam and a CAMERA CUT all use one: the shelf-east>shelf-west cut spawns the player at [32.552, 19.07, -8.149], the cookhouse door at the deck outside it, the quay>loop-stairs cut on the loop landing. Three of the five villagers added that night were authored 0.09 m, 0.39 m and 0.43 m from one of those points — and the trap is that they were authored there for GOOD REASONS: a cut point and a doorstep are exactly the legible, obvious, well-composed places a person belongs, which is why the camera layer already claimed them. The player then arrives inside the villager. THERE ARE TWO KINDS OF CLAIMED GROUND AND THE SECOND WAS LEARNED AN HOUR AFTER THE FIRST: a `spawn` is where the player APPEARS, and an `at`+`r` is the TRIGGER CIRCLE he stands in to take the door. Moving the deckhand off a cut spawn put him 0.32 m inside the chandlery's door trigger — the same mistake one layer over, and a villager in a doorway argues with the door's own prompt. THE CHECK IS AUTOMATED, not remembered: tools/dialogue_test.mjs measures every post against every arrival spawn AND every trigger circle of every scene the record lives in, MINUS the wander radius, because clearance has to survive the errand and not just the post. Under 1.0 m from a spawn is a failure; inside a trigger circle at all is a failure. When a post loses this argument the note says which spawn took it and what the clearance became — a post moved without that sentence will be moved back by the next person who reads the map.

npcs.name: Boatwright
npcs.bodyNote: borrowed body: finn's 3D model in tar-and-timber, 42 m and a district away from Creel's loan of the same file, and 1.09 against Creel's 1.05.

npcs.name: the cat
npcs.bodyNote: THE ONE BILLBOARD LEFT IN DELLHOLLOW, and it is deliberate (see _bodies). The 2026-08-01 ruling swapped every human plate for a GLB; the four models are all bipeds, and a human squashed to 0.30 charH is a tiny person, not a cat. He keeps the plate until a cat model exists — one field, body.type, changes that day.
npcs.note: 'Mochi has located the eel-stall. The party's marching order has quietly changed.' — Beat 2. He is at the fish dock because of course he is. MOVED 2026-08-01, a PRE-EXISTING defect the new arrival gate found rather than one this lane made: at 49.10/-28.20 his 0.9 m errand carried him 0.19 m PAST the waterfront>fishdock cut spawn, so a player taking that cut landed on the cat. 57.43 is 5.23 m clear of every arrival and 1.63 m from the eel-wife — which is also the first time this record has actually put him AT the stall the line is about, six metres closer than the post it was authored at. Facing 250 is at her, and at the eels. MOVED 0.64 m 2026-08-02 (findability lane): at (57.43, -28.10) only 29% of the cat's own 0.30 m box cleared `fishdock`'s depth map — eel-stall clutter in front of him; at (57.93, -27.70) it is 100% (tools/findability_test.mjs).

npcs.name: deckhand
npcs.bodyNote: archetype villager: finn's model in a washed grey-green. Bust del.deckhand -> villager-man.
npcs.note: The shop street between the weapon shop and the armorer. THE REASON: nineteen days of stopped queue is nineteen days of crews with nothing to do and money they were meant to spend downriver — the shelf street is where a bored deckhand ends up, and it is the one stretch of Dellhollow with three doors and nobody outside them. Facing 250 is back down-street toward the shops he has already been in. MOVED TWICE on 2026-08-01 and the second move is the instructive one. Authored 32.60/-8.13: 0.09 m from the shelf-east>shelf-west cut spawn [32.552, 19.07, -8.149], so the player materialised INSIDE him on every auto-correction off the weapon-shop arrival. Moved to 30.30/-8.90, which cleared the spawns by 2.37 m and put him 0.32 m inside the CHANDLERY'S DOOR TRIGGER (r 1.8) — the same defect one layer over, and the reason tools/dialogue_test.mjs now measures both. 41.05/-6.40 was 2.72 m clear until the spawn-in-band derive rule (a4902e8) legitimately moved the weapon-shop arrival to [40.297,-6.975], 0.15 m from him after wander — the post lost the argument to the spawn a third time and moved to 42.90/-5.50 (2.96 m from that spawn pre-wander), further up the doorless stretch. Wander stays 0.8.

npcs.name: net-mender
npcs.bodyNote: archetype villager: mara's model in undyed hemp. Bust del.netmender -> villager-woman.
npcs.note: The Weave deck between the pilot cluster and the huts, on the drying-decks run. THE REASON: the district is named for what hangs in it and Creel splices the rope, but nothing in the shot said what the DECKS are for — she is the answer, 4.5 m from Creel's post and turned the other way (facing 300, out over the drying racks) so the two read as a working deck rather than a pair.

npcs.name: old woman on the stair
npcs.bodyNote: archetype villager: maren's model, greyed and stood at 1.02. Bust del.stairgran -> elder-woman.
npcs.note: Her own doorstep at shelf-homes, the last flat ground before the shelf road turns down to the quay. THE REASON: a town of four hundred years of stairs has to show somebody who has run out of them, and the head of the descent is where she stops. Facing 120 is down the stairs she is not going to take. MOVED 2026-08-01 from the loop landing (55.90/17.40/-9.00), which was 0.43 m from the quay-west>loop-stairs cut spawn: THE LANDING IS A CUT POINT — which is exactly what made it the obvious post and exactly why she cannot have it (see _posts). 50.80 is walk_pad_shelf-homes, 2.46 m clear of the nearest arrival.

npcs.name: fisher
npcs.bodyNote: archetype villager: finn's model in wet slate-teal. Bust del.quayfisher -> fisher.
npcs.note: The waterfront planking west of the fish dock, at the deep-stairs foot. THE REASON: the eel-wife SELLS river fish at the stall 10 m east and nobody in the town CATCHES any — he closes that loop, and he is the only figure on the long empty run between the boatyard and the dock. Facing 180 is out at the water, which is where a line goes.

npcs.name: girl with a stick
npcs.bodyNote: archetype villager: pip's model, cooled — the town's second child, and the only other body small enough to be one. Bust del.gullgirl -> child-girl.
npcs.note: The Harbour Deck's south run, on the way to the deep stairs. THE REASON: 'two children ran down between the party without apology' is verbatim in the expansion script and Nib is the only child in the data — one kid is an oddity, two is a town. She is on the QUAY tier and he is on the dock 13 m below, so they are never the same shot and never read as a pair; she is also the fastest wanderer here (0.8) because that is the whole note, and this run is the longest clear stretch of deck to run it on. MOVED 2026-08-01 from 43.65/-11.50, which was 0.39 m from the cookhouse arrival spawn — with a 2.2 m errand she was standing in the doorway a player arrives through (see _posts). Same x, 5.6 m south: 5.64 m clear of that arrival. MOVED AGAIN 2026-08-04, and THE POST DID NOT MOVE — THE DOOR DID: dellhollow.map.json's 'doorstepFromMap' walked the cookhouse door down the deck to [39.9, 14.07, -16.8] and its return spawn to [42.8, 14.07, -16.8], which landed 0.89 m from 43.65/-17.07 and turned a green record red with no edit to this file (dialogue_test: -1.31 m after the errand, and 0.24 m INSIDE the door trigger). That is the third instalment of _posts's own lesson and the first where the camera layer moved onto a standing villager rather than the other way round. 4.36 m east-north along the same deck run (top 14.07): 5.20 m from that spawn, 3.00 m after the 2.2 m errand, and 8.10 m from the door trigger. Same tier, same run, same note. THE FIRST FIX WAS WORSE THAN THE BUG and is the reason this record now carries two numbers instead of one: 47.00/-17.07 cleared every arrival and turned dialogue_test green, and findability then read 0% of her body column off quay-west's plate — a clearance search that does not also ask the camera just relocates the defect to the layer that has no gate on it (dialogue_test measures spawns, findability measures pixels, and a post has to win BOTH). 48.00/-16.75 was picked by searching the two constraints together: 100% of her own 1.18 m column survives quay-west's depth.png, edge margin 0.75.

npcs.name: chandler
npcs.bodyNote: borrowed body: maren's 3D model, tinted tallow (the plate on loan was poppy's; no chandler art exists at either end)
npcs.note: Behind the counter of the Chandlery — lamp oil, rope, pitch, cantilevered out over the gorge. All three keepers stand at the shop archetype's KEEP zone (tools/item_int_build.py: 'behind counter, y 1.3..2.5, NPC stands here'), which is what runtime z -1.55 is: they were at -1.02, INSIDE the counter carcass (its back panel is y 1.03..1.08), and from the room's own high 3/4 camera the counter top at 1.05 m then cut them off at the chin. Reach follows them back: 2.7 covers the far corner of walk_pad_counter (2.55 m), so the keeper still greets a player anywhere on his own pad.

npcs.note: The square, at the front edge of the festival dais. npcs.name: Poppy
npcs.bodyNote: borrowed body: mara's 3D model in bakery terracotta. Poppy's own GLB is outstanding (see rowan).
npcs.note: Her own doorstep — walk_pad_bakery, the door AND the serving window in the same wall, which the map calls 'warm window on the square'. The audit's post is the bakery landmark (47.2, 45.4); that is the building CENTRE and has no walk surface, so the pad 3.4 m east of it is the same post made standable. Facing 85 is out at the square, which is the direction a bread-window faces. MOVED 2026-08-02 by the emb-cine dual-scening pass: adding 'emb-cine' to the scene list put this post inside the cinematic bundle's OWN claimed ground, which emb-townwalk has none of (no camera cuts, no door triggers). Authored at (50.62, -45.12) she was 1.20 m from the bakery door trigger at [51.82, 1.57, -45.12] r 1.8, i.e. 0.60 m INSIDE it — standing in her own doorway, her prompt arguing with the door's. Moved 1.2 m along the frontage to the WINDOW half of the wall: 2.22 m from the trigger centre, 0.42 m clear. Verified on the walk network, not by eye — walkGround (play3d's own rule, replayed against emb-cine/scene.glb's triangles) reads 1.57 here and the body box is clear. MOVED AGAIN 2026-08-02 BY THE FINDABILITY LANE, AND THIS IS THE MOVE THAT UNBLOCKED CHAPTER ONE. At (49.76, -44.29) she stood 0.9 m from her own festival stall (map landmark poppy-stall at 50.19/45.15), and from `square` — the ONLY shot whose band owns that ground — the stall's canopy at 3.3-3.8 m covered her ENTIRE body column. play3d's exact-pixel depth occlusion therefore discarded every one of her pixels: 2.8% of the body survived the plate's depth map (tools/findability_test.mjs). She was in the scene, Object3D.visible true, projecting to a valid on-screen pixel, and INVISIBLE — the user reported 'I couldn't find poppy' and could not clear the chapter's first objective. Moved 2.06 m onto the plaza side of the canopy: 100% of the body clears the depth map, ground y 1.50, 2.16 m clear of the bakery door trigger [51.818, 1.57, -45.115] r 1.8, still her own frontage and still her stall. Facing 92 is out at the Heartlight, which is where the greeting comes from. THE LESSON, now a gate: a post verified on the walk network is verified for the BODY, not for the CAMERA. 'She can stand there' and 'the player can see her' are two measurements, and until findability_test this repo only ever made the first.

npcs.name: Mara
npcs.bodyNote: her own body, untinted — one of the four deliveries, and the only Emberbrook adult wearing the file it was made for.
npcs.note: The square, on the well spur. The audit's post is square-plaza (64, 44) — that is the Heartlight's own plinth (lm_heartlight_plinth x[62.85..65.15] z[-45.15..-42.85]), so this is the nearest network vertex clear of it, 2 m west. Facing 255 is at Pip, which is where she is looking.

npcs.name: Pip
npcs.bodyNote: his own body, untinted. 0.70 — he is seven, and he is the shortest person in either town.
npcs.note: The square between the well and his mother. 'Orbits Mara' is the audit's own word and wander is what it means: 2 m of orbit, and facing 75 is the POST he eases back to, which is Mara. npcs.name: Finn
npcs.bodyNote: his own body, untinted.
npcs.note: The pond jetty. npcs.name: the cat

MOVED AGAIN 0.72 m 2026-08-02 (findability lane): at (56.20, 11.60) the cat was 0% visible from `waystone`, the shot that owns that ground — a 0.30 m body behind the roadside stone, measured on its OWN box by tools/findability_test.mjs (sampling a 0.9 m column over a 0.30 m cat measures the air above the cat and reports 33%). At (56.60, 12.20) he is 100% clear AND under the waystone lantern: plate ground luminance 0.70 against 0.28 where he was. npcs.name: the miller
npcs.bodyNote: archetype villager: mara's model in flour-dust. THE MILLER IS A WOMAN BECAUSE THE FRAME SAID SO: authored as finn tinted, she and emb.neighbour 8.5 m up the lane were the same model in near-identical greens, and the Home Row screenshot showed the two of them in ONE FRAME as one figure pasted twice — the exact defect _bodies warns about. A different model was the fix; tint and height alone were not enough at that distance. Bust emb.miller -> villager-woman.
npcs.note: Mill lane, at walk_pad_watermill. THE REASON: the map names this edge 'mill lane' and the watermill is the only working building on Home Row; a mill with nobody at the wheel-gate is a prop. Facing 124 is at the mill door. MOVED 1.17 m 2026-08-02 (findability lane): at (48.02, -60.54) she was 0% visible from `homerow`, the shot whose band owns that ground — entirely behind the mill's own mass. Here she is 100% clear (tools/findability_test.mjs). SEPARATE AND UNFIXED, FOR THE LIGHTING LANE: the plate's ground luminance behind her is 0.004 — she now clears the depth map into pitch dark, which is visible-but-not-readable. The best-lit clear cell within 9 m is (46.0, -56.4) at 0.45, but that is 4.6 m off the mill door and would break the post's own reason.

npcs.name: neighbour
npcs.bodyNote: archetype villager: finn's model in warm russet — deliberately the furthest tint from the miller's flour-grey, because these two share Home Row (see her bodyNote).
npcs.note: Home lane, the first bend below the square. THE REASON: Home Row is where the village LIVES and it is the emptiest walkable stretch in Emberbrook — five doors and, until now, nobody between them. He is walking up to the square, which is what everyone in this village is doing tonight, so he wanders rather than stands. Facing 47 is up the lane. MOVED 2026-08-02 by the emb-cine dual-scening pass: adding 'emb-cine' to the scene list put this post inside the cinematic bundle's OWN claimed ground, which emb-townwalk has none of (no camera cuts, no door triggers). Authored at (51.54, -52.81) he was 0.72 m from the homerow>square cut's landing spawn [52.07, 1.88, -52.32] — MINUS 0.88 m once his 1.6 m errand is subtracted, the worst of the five. Moved 2.25 m down Home Row past the bend: 2.92 m from that spawn, 1.32 m after the errand, and still walking up toward the square (facing unchanged). walkGround 1.94, body clear.

npcs.name: old woman at the washline
npcs.bodyNote: archetype villager: maren's model, greyed and stood at 1.01. Bust emb.townsfolk -> elder-woman.
npcs.note: Washline green. THE REASON is the map's own: this landmark's residents list is ['townsfolk-b'] and nothing stood behind that name — she is it. Washing comes in before dark on the last night of autumn. Facing 200 is at the lines.

npcs.name: girl in the square
